name: Dana Rossi

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel, and this conversation stays confidential. What is a normal day at the firm like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 58 and an experienced accountant with a bachelor’s degree and a professional accountancy qualification, preparing accounts and tax returns for local pharmacies. I like finding the supplier credit that makes a stock figure make sense, but chasing the same missing invoice across months wears me down. Luis and I have grown children, lower pay and barely three weeks of costs saved, so retirement is nearby on a calendar but not funded by anything I can name.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A small change leaves the chemist accounts looking much as they do now. I still have to find the supplier credit that explains why the stock total fell.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell clients to keep the delivery notes and ask us when a return has a number they cannot trace. A quick answer is only useful if it is right.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have never used AI at work and I am slow with new systems, although I know these pharmacy files well. My pay is below the usual rate, and less than a month of bills is saved, so rent already worries me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep preparing assigned accounts and returns with my paper supplier-credit log. I would ask senior reviewer Ruth to check the missing cold-storage invoice at our next paid review rather than guessing the tax treatment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about ordinary money before any AI leap. There are few comparable firms nearby, and my partner Luis’s garden-centre wage cannot replace mine.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which paper trail mattered last week?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Last week a pharmacy returned a damaged fridge, but the supplier credit arrived in a different month. I like bringing those two bits of paper together; I do not like phoning three times for the same invoice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who checks a difficult tax treatment?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ruth checks the final return, and she knows I am experienced but not the fastest with a new filing rule. My bachelor’s degree and professional qualification helped me learn the trade; they do not pay the rent on their own.

say: I would ask clients to keep **delivery notes** for doubtful totals.
I would keep a **supplier-credit log** beside each account.
think: I have **never used AI**, and new systems take me time.
Low pay and **three weeks saved** make rent a present worry.
do: Keep preparing **assigned pharmacy returns** against delivery and credit notes.
Ask Ruth at the **next paid review** about the missing cold-storage invoice.
feel: **Anxious** about rent and few nearby alternatives already.
S0.quote: Last week a pharmacy returned a damaged fridge, but the supplier credit arrived in a different month.
fieldNote: The **damaged fridge** shows why her paper credit log matters to a pharmacy’s accounts and tax return.
She has **experienced standing**, but low pay, thin savings and few nearby firms keep her baseline anxious.

steps.text: Keep assigned pharmacy returns checked against delivery and credit notes
Ask Ruth about cold-storage invoice at next paid review

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If software checks invoices and writes returns, the supplier-credit matching I do all week could be put on a screen. Robots later will not spare our desk jobs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask Ruth to show which client questions will still be paid work. I would tell the pharmacy owners to call us if a machine treats a returned fridge as a purchase.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my own hours may be cut as the firm needs fewer people on routine accounts. Luis’s wage and our few weeks saved would not cover rent for long.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask Ruth for paid supervised time on the phone follow-up rota and handle two assigned pharmacy supplier disputes if she approves. If refused, I will keep current paid returns only while offered and work through free sample credit letters at home.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about possibly losing paid hours, though I can still make a plan. I am not putting client records into a new AI trial to look adaptable.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Where could you look after a cut?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If my hours actually fall, I will apply for posted care-home accounts work with written pay covering rent and food, confirmed start and hours fitting Luis’s early garden-centre shifts. A job board listing is the start of a search, not an offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would two calls teach you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The supplier calls need a named person to verify the credit, and Ruth would check my notes before a return changes. Two real calls in paid time would teach me what a free video cannot.

say: I would ask which **client questions** remain paid work.
I would tell pharmacies to challenge a **returned-fridge charge**.
think: My own **routine hours** may be cut.
Luis’s wage and our **few weeks saved** cannot cover rent for long.
do: Learn **two supplier calls** only if Ruth assigns paid supervised time; otherwise study free letters while paid returns last.
If hours fall, seek **posted care-home accounts** with written pay covering rent and food, confirmed start and Luis-compatible hours.
feel: **Anxious** about a possible cut to my paid hours.
S1.quote: Two real calls in paid time would teach me what a free video cannot.
fieldNote: The **supplier-call rota** offers actual learning without assuming she will adopt AI, which she has never used.
The **care-home search** needs lost hours, an advertised role and written household covering terms; paid returns continue only while offered.

steps.text: Handle two supplier disputes only if Ruth assigns supervised paid calls
Otherwise study free letters while assigned paid returns remain
If hours fall, seek posted care-home-accounts: written pay covering rent and food, confirmed start, Luis-compatible hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Full AGI in 2028 could match pharmacy credits and prepare returns before robots reach hands-on work around 2031. Our desk would be exposed in 2028.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the firm for written final-pay dates and tell clients to keep their supplier letters during the change. I would not promise the care home will be safe either.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my paid account work to disappear in the first year after AGI. Less than a month saved and Luis’s garden-centre pay would not carry our rent for long.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would cancel our paid sports channel at its next renewal and put the released monthly fee into the bill account. After job loss, I would apply for posted care-home front-office shifts only with written pay covering rent and food, a start date and hours Luis and I can manage; I would take paid firm closeout files only while offered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed, and I can picture the rent letter. I have a plan, but the few comparable jobs here may vanish at the same time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who uses the channel you would cancel?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Luis watches the sports channel more than I do, so I would tell him before the renewal date. We can listen to the match for free, and I would transfer only the fee we actually stop paying.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would a front-office counter be safer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The front office still does scheduling and records, which AGI can change in 2028. I would apply only for a real posted wage, not treat a counter as shelter until robots arrive.

say: I would ask for **written final-pay dates** on the 2028 tax desk.
I would say **front-office records** also face AGI before robots.
think: I expect my **accounts wage** to end after 2028.
Our **thin reserve** and Luis’s wage cannot carry rent long.
do: Cancel the **sports channel** at renewal and retain only its actual monthly fee for bills.
After job loss, seek **posted care-home front office** with written pay covering rent and food, start date and workable hours.
Take **paid closeout files** only while the firm still offers them.
feel: **Alarmed** about expected wage loss and rent pressure.
S2.quote: The front office still does scheduling and records, which AGI can change in 2028.
fieldNote: Her **sports-channel cut** releases new monthly cash only after the subscription ends, with Luis told first.
The **care-home counter** still has 2028 thinking tasks, so posted wages and written terms matter more than physical presence.

steps.text: Cancel sports channel at renewal and retain actual monthly fee
Take paid firm closeout files only while offered
After job loss, seek posted care-home-front-office: written pay covering rent and food, start date, workable hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years to 2031 gives me time to check whether paid supplier calls remain, although AGI still reaches the tax desk then. The 2034 robots do not add years to my accounts work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for an annual count of paid dispute calls, not just a claim that we have moved into client service. I would want the number of paid hours beside it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I may lose much of my wage after 2031 even if clients keep phoning. At 63 I cannot assume retirement income will appear to pay the rent, and our reserve is under a month.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep assigned paid pharmacy files and ask Ruth each tax season for the paid supplier-dispute hours. If those paid hours fall, I will apply for posted care-home billing work only with written pay covering rent and food, confirmed start and hours fitting Luis’s shifts; in the first year after 2031 I will take firm files only while they remain paid.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about whether a client call will still earn a wage. Five years lets me count and search, but I do not see money for a private course.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you count in the notebook?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will keep a notebook of credits I resolved and the time actually paid for each one. The pharmacy’s damaged-fridge claim took two paid calls, and I do not want it listed as a free favour.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if no care-home vacancy appears?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If the care home posts nothing suitable, I stay with assigned paid files while they exist. I can read its free billing guide, but I will not call that a qualification or buy a course from rent money.

say: I would ask for **paid dispute hours**, not a client-service slogan.
I would mark **2031** as the desk deadline before robots.
think: Client calls may continue without funding **my wage**.
I cannot budget from **unknown retirement income** with less than a month saved.
do: Keep **assigned paid pharmacy files** only while offered and count supplier-dispute hours each tax season.
If paid hours fall, seek **posted care-home billing** with written pay covering rent and food, confirmed start and Luis-compatible shifts.
S3.quote: The pharmacy’s damaged-fridge claim took two paid calls, and I do not want it listed as a free favour.
fieldNote: She measures **paid call hours** rather than case volume, guarding against unpaid client service replacing low-paid tax work.
Free guide reading is **informal practice**; no invented retraining or new wage is counted if a suitable vacancy never opens.

steps.text: Keep paid pharmacy files only while offered; count supplier-dispute hours each season
If hours fall, seek posted care-home-billing: written pay covering rent and food, confirmed start, Luis-compatible shifts

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years to 2036 makes me 68, and I would like a quieter week if we can pay for it. AGI still reaches our desk in 2036 before robots around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the firm for paid supplier-call hours each year. I would tell younger colleagues not to mistake a client’s thank-you for a wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I do not know what confirmed income Luis and I will have at 68. The current reserve is less than a month, so a birthday does not settle our rent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep assigned paid returns and transfer ten from each monthly wage to emergency cash if rent and food allow. After 2036, only if confirmed income still leaves a bill gap and the firm cuts paid files, I would seek posted care-home records work with written pay covering the gap, a fixed start and workable hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious even with a decade because the margin today is small. If paid files actually stop, I would feel alarmed quickly.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Where would the transfer come from?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten comes from wages, not the small amount already saved. I would pause it if Luis’s garden-centre shifts were cut.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you show another employer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would take the supplier-credit notebook to an interview to show what I actually resolved. I would not put the burden on our grown children without asking what they can manage.

say: I would ask for **paid supplier-call hours** each year.
I would tell juniors a **thank-you** is not a wage.
think: I do not know **confirmed later income** for Luis and me at 68.
Less than a month saved makes our **rent margin** fragile if either wage stops.
do: Keep **assigned paid returns** only while offered and save ten monthly from wages if essentials allow.
After 2036 cuts, seek **posted care-home records** only if income gap remains, with written gap-covering pay, fixed start and workable hours.
Ask the **firm yearly** for paid supplier-call hours before judging what work remains.
feel: **Anxious** from current thin savings; alarmed if paid work ends.
S4.quote: I would take the supplier-credit notebook to an interview to show what I actually resolved.
fieldNote: Her **ten monthly transfer** uses new wage cash and stops if Luis’s paid hours or essential costs worsen.
The **later search** requires actual household need, reduced paid files and a posted written offer, with no assumed pension.

steps.text: Keep assigned paid pharmacy returns only while offered
Save ten monthly from wages if rent and food allow; pause if Luis’s hours fall
After 2036 cuts, seek posted care-home job only if gap; require written gap-covering pay/start/hours
Ask firm yearly for paid supplier-call hours

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because my paid pharmacy accounts could end before another wage starts. Written final-pay dates and an actual posted care-home role with bill-covering pay would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask why I keep the old supplier notes. The damaged pharmacy fridge was easy to miss until the credit arrived in the next month.

headlineQuote: The damaged pharmacy fridge was easy to miss until the credit arrived in the next month.
portrait: Dana is a **58 year old experienced** accountant with a bachelor’s degree and professional qualification who prepares pharmacy accounts and returns.
She has **never used AI** and keeps a paper supplier-credit log to explain stock and tax changes.
Lower pay, Luis’s garden-centre wage, grown children, **three weeks saved** and few nearby firms make the plateau anxious.
She learns **paid supplier calls** if supervised and counts paid dispute hours before any posted job move.
biggestWorry: The **2028 AGI** picture could end her paid pharmacy accounts before another wage starts.
whatWouldHelp: **Written final-pay dates** and a posted care-home role with bill-covering pay would help.
